transcription.notes: Problems page 2 is the answer sheet (Naked Eye Observational Round Answer Sheet, Student ID, Chart) and is attached as the figure of Problem 1. Printed "label the accordingly" (Problem 1) is kept verbatim (a wrong word, not a non-word). The solutions document gives only grading criteria; the solution charts on pages 2, 3 and 5 print "Nova Sagitarii" (kept in figures). The Messier table header prints "Magnitudo" and lists Messier 20 twice (6.3/29 and 6.9/11), both kept verbatim. Solutions page 6 is blank. The official solution for Problem 2 and Problem 3 refers to the circles on the chart of solutions page 2 (attached to Problem 1's solution); the five brightest stars are numbered 1–5 there and the Moon is circled in green. No numeric value for the Nunki–Shaula distance is printed, so no answer is given for Problem 6. No paper total is printed (problem points sum to 100).

problems.statement:
In the blank square given in the answer sheet, you should assume that Nova Sagittarii 2 is in the center. (marked by green star)

RA(J2000) : 18h 36m 56.84s

Dec(J2000) : -28$^{\circ}$ 55’ 39.8”

Draw Declination and Right Ascension lines passing through Nova Sagittarii. Also draw parallel gridlines at convenient interval and label the accordingly. (The field of view is 45$^{\circ}$) (10 points)

figures.alt: Answer sheet chart: a blank square frame with a green star marking Nova Sagittarii 2 at the center, a north arrow labelled N in the upper right corner and the label FOV 45° at the lower right edge.

solution.statement: Dec and RA grids made, Full Score

figures.alt: Official solution sky chart of Sagittarius and Scorpius with RA lines 17h, 18h00m, 19h00m and declination circles -10°00’, -20°00’, -30°00’, -40°00’; red lines through Nova Sagitarii at 18h 36m 56.84s and -28° 55’ 39.8”; the Galactic Plane drawn as a line; Messier objects labelled M 6 to M 75; the Moon enclosed by green dashed concentric circles; five bright stars marked 1–5 with red dashed concentric circles.
